label: signs certificate for
type: subject = a certificate (root or intermediate) acting as issuer; object = the certificate kind it issues. Expresses one hop of a certificate chain.
note: Completes the certificate family's shape. verifiesIdentityOf (already promoted) points from a trust store to the party it validates - the RUNTIME check; this points from an issuer to what it issues - the ISSUANCE structure. Both were needed and only the first existed, which is why the registry could describe certificate validation but not certificate hierarchy: it had no way to say that an intermediate certificate signs node, client and further intermediate certificates, which is the fact every rotation procedure depends on.
relates_to_competency_question: What can each kind of certificate in the chain issue?
